gaps: The capture contains two programs: the complete BS in Environmental Health and Safety (ledgered here) and the opening of the BS in Finance. If the Finance program was intended, its 42 credits of Required Business Core Courses are not itemized in the capture, so a complete Finance ledger cannot be built from it.

The program table does not state how the 78 'Remaining General Education and Elective Courses' credits split between general education and electives. The general education total is 41 credits (Communications 12, Mathematics 3, Arts and Humanities 6, Behavioral and Social Sciences 6, Biological and Physical Sciences 7, Research and Computing Literacy 7). The related courses MATH 115 and CHEM 297 may be applied to general education, but the exact remaining general-education versus elective breakdown is not printed for this program.

Residency is stated only as overall policy, not per course: at least 30 credits (normally the final 30) must be completed at UMGC, half the credits within the major must be completed at UMGC, and at least 15 upper-level credits (300–499) must be completed at UMGC. The capture does not say which specific courses must be taken at UMGC.
The minimum grade of C applies to major courses. WRTG 112 must be earned with a C- or better within the first 24 credits. These grade rules are not captured as ledger lines.

The specific course requirements for the general-education sub-blocks (for example WRTG 112 and an upper-level advanced writing course) appear only in the general section. The program's course sequencing lists recommended rather than required courses for these blocks.

upperLevelMinimum.basis: UMGC’s bachelor’s degree requirements set no degree-wide upper-level minimum. Their only upper-level rule is 15 upper-level credits (courses numbered 300 to 499) completed at UMGC. This plan’s named upper-level courses with no outside option total 36 credits, so it meets that rule.
